title: HKMA Completes e-HKD Pilot Programme and Outlines Future Direction of e-HKD
summary: On 28 October 2025, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced that it had completed the e-HKD Pilot Programme -- its staged exploration of a potential Hong Kong dollar central bank digital currency -- and set out the initiative's future direction. HKMA said the immediate priority for e-HKD now lies beyond retail use cases, redirecting near-term focus toward wholesale payments and toward supporting Hong Kong's wider tokenisation ecosystem, an effort it brands e-HKD+. HKMA did not commit to a specific timetable for a possible future retail e-HKD, describing further preparatory work on that question as ongoing. e-HKD is one strand of HKMA's broader work on tokenised forms of money, alongside its separate work on tokenised bank deposits.
why_it_matters: For a newcomer, this announcement marks Hong Kong's central-bank-style regulator concluding a phase of retail digital-currency experimentation and redirecting its near-term digital-money efforts toward the banking system's wholesale and institutional plumbing rather than a Hong Kong dollar available directly to the public.
